## Short description

A quiet pixel-art winter road that lives through your real day — and a little snowplough clears it every morning.

## Description (paste into the store's description box)

A fully procedural pixel-art wallpaper: an empty snowy county road, two old streetlamps, a leaning utility pole and
buried fence posts — drawn entirely by one GPU shader, no images. It is almost still. Things happen slowly.

**It follows your real day.** Sunrise, sunset and the sun's position are calculated for your location (set your
latitude/longitude in the settings). The whole scene swaps between hand-picked pixel-art palettes for night, dawn,
day and dusk: cold blue nights, a rose dawn, clear winter-blue days, mauve dusks.

**Little things:**
- Snow falls in three depth layers and is nearly invisible in the dark — it only shows where it drifts through the lamplight
- The streetlamps switch off after sunrise and stutter back on at dusk; now and then one flickers (the far one is dying)
- Through the night snow builds on the road, the fog thickens and the fence sinks…
- …until ~25 minutes after sunrise, when a tiny plough with an amber beacon crawls up the road and clears it
  (impatient? there's a **Send the plough** button in the settings)
- Wind drifts through calm, drift and gust moods; snowfall comes and goes in patches

**Two monitors?** Set the monitor above to **Scene: Sky** — the real moon in its current phase behind drifting snow
clouds at night, the sun crossing a winter sky by day. Both screens share one clock, so the wind and snow match.

**Light:** ~1–3 % of one CPU core (everything runs on the GPU).

**Settings:** scene (road / sky), pixel size, frame rate, snow, fog, wind, lamp flicker, winter mode
(follows the day / always clear / always buried), latitude & longitude, preview any hour, send the plough.

Requires Plasma 6. Install from *Desktop and Wallpaper → Get New Plugins…*, or manually:
`kpackagetool6 -t Plasma/Wallpaper -i silent-county-road-1.1.tar.gz`

**1.0** — First release: night scene, lamplit snow, the road that disappears through the night.
